thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 1865009999 — High CPU + OOM on tokenizer pods in prod-us-west-2. Multiple pods in CrashLoopBackOff / OOMKilled. Paging @oncall-elena and @eng-runtime-pager :rotating_light:

oncall-elena: seeing the page, jumping in. any immediate customer impact numbers?

devon: Pager fired at 23:12. Cloud metrics show tokenizer preproc CPU at 95% on the node pool for ~10m, kernel OOM messages starting at 23:15. A few pods got OOMKilled.

sanjay: looking at logs — tokenizer service (tokenize-worker) shows a big surge in single-request token count, ~>50k tokens per request. That's blowing out user-space memory during tokenization. Not seeing GPU allocation spikes. This looks CPU/memory on the node.

kai: forwarding `kubectl get pods` for the tokenizer deployment:
```
NAME                                 READY   STATUS      RESTARTS   AGE
tokenize-worker-5b7d9c8f6-2m9pz      0/1     OOMKilled   3          2h
tokenize-worker-5b7d9c8f6-h6qz2      0/1     CrashLoopBackOff  5    2h
tokenize-worker-5b7d9c8f6-jk7lm      1/1     Running     0          18m
```

mira: dmesg extract from node ip-10-0-4-12 (trimmed):
```
Out of memory: Killed process 21457 (python) total-vm:4800000kB, anon-rss:3500000kB
Memory cgroup out of memory: kill process 21457 (python) uid 1001 pgtables: 0
```

opsbot: Autoscaler tried to add 2 nodes at 23:20 but provisioning delayed by instance quota.

devon: customer-success FYI — we're seeing increased 5xxs on generate endpoint, roughly 6% error rate over last 12m, top affected customers: cust-132, cust-554 (high volume) — CS reaching out.

customer-success: yep we already opened DRI contact for cust-132, they're seeing ~30% failure on long prompts. They've flagged as P2.

oncall-elena: initial mitigation plan: 1) scale tokenizer replicas down to 0.5 traffic via rollout weight (route small fraction to fallback model), 2) apply emergency env var to cap tokenizer max_tokens_per_batch to 4096, 3) cordon the noisy node and drain (to avoid further OOMs), 4) request quota bump or spin standby nodes. Who can run the emergency rollout? @kai / @devon?

kai: I can push the emergency config. Preparing a canary patch that sets MAX_TOKENS=4096 and adds a per-request token count guard. Will push + restart one replica first.

sanjay: also recommend enabling model fallback in routing for heavy requests: route anything with token_count>4k to smaller model variant (quantized) to preserve latency. I'll open the routing override.

opsbot: Quota request submitted to cloud: increase vCPU quota in us-west-2 by 8. Ticket #CLOUD-7891. ETA 20–40m.

kai: rolling out patch to tokenizer image (emergency tag `tokenizer:emergency-20260315`) and setting env MAX_TOKENS=4096. Applying to 1/3 replicas as canary now.

(23:36) kai: canary restarted, tokenization now includes quick-reject for >4k tokens with 413 response and a short explanatory header.

mira: logs show the canary honored the limit — sample request with 60k tokens got rejected fast, and CPU stayed below 60% for that pod.

oncall-elena: starting gradual rollout to remaining pods. Monitor CPU + OOM counts. Also initiating node cordon/drain on ip-10-0-4-12 to move any stateful work off the noisy node.

(23:44) devon: node drained, moved pods to new nodes. New pods coming up healthy. No further OOMKilled messages after 23:40.

(23:52) opsbot: Autoscaler succeeded — 2 new nodes are ready.

(00:05) devon: observed error rate drop from 6% -> 1.2% after canary + rollout + node drain + autoscale. Affected customer cust-132 reporting improvement.

customer-success: confirmed cust-132 now down to ~2% failure, they're ok with the current mitigation. Keeping them informed.

oncall-elena: immediate mitigation status: throttling in place, rollout complete, node cordoned/drained, autoscale succeeded. Impact: degraded for long-prompt customers for ~25m, ~6% errors at peak. No evidence of CUDA GPU errors — this was CPU OOM driven by tokenization hot path.

sanjay: root cause hypothesis: a sudden spike of malformed/very-long prompts bypassed upstream length validation and triggered a pathological tokenization workload (hotloop). Our tokenizer allocates proportional data structures and a pathological length caused multi-GB transient allocations leading to cgroup OOMKills.

mira: quick diff of tokenizer change we rolled: added early guard in request parsing and defensive `try/except` around token buffer allocations, and set a hard allocator cap.

kai: follow-ups we need to track in a postmortem: 1) add upstream prompt-length validation + reject at ingress, 2) limit per-request tokenizer memory via RLIMIT/ulimit and in-process checks, 3) add per-user rate limiting for extremely long prompts, 4) improve autoscaler to pre-provision for sudden bursts, 5) add perf tests for extreme token counts. I'll own 1 & 2.

eng-runtime-pager: escalate to runtime eng for clarifying memory accounting on the tokenizer container and whether we can make tokenization streaming to reduce peak memory. Assigning to @sanjay and @kai.

(00:22) non-urgent note: open a support incident for cust-554 (lower-tier but high throughput) to offer guidance on prompt size. customer-success will coordinate.

oncall-elena: handing off to daytime SRE — I'm going to sleep. Handoff notes: rollout tag `tokenizer:emergency-20260315` in prod, canary verified, nodes scaled, quota ticket CLOUD-7891 pending. Postmortem owner: kai. Please escalate if OOMs reappear.

kai: acknowledged handoff. I will create the postmortem doc and link logs/traces.

incident-bot: Incident 1865009999 status -> mitigated. Follow-up required: postmortem, perf tests, routing validation.

mira: saving logs and dmesg snippets to /var/log/incidents/1865009999.log and linking to the postmortem.

sanjay: quick note for root cause doc: include snippet of offending request pattern (redacted) and token count histogram for the hour.

customer-success: marking impacted customers list in ticketing system and noting mitigation details for post-incident outreach.

devon: thanks team. I'll watch the alerting for the next 6 hours and ping if any regression.

oncall-elena: good work everyone :thumbsup: — restoring normal ops.
